title: Ops→SE Fast Handoff: Pilot Enablement Mini-Deck (Draft)
body:
Slide 1 — One-line purpose:
  Quick kit for Operations -> Sales Engineering handoffs during rapid pilot onramps (focus: private/dedicated deployments). Draft / working notes, not final.

Slide 2 — TL;DR for SEs:
  - What Ops will guarantee for pilot: reserved baseline throughput, canary window, telemetry hooks, rollback plan.
  - What SE must deliver: test prompts, sample traffic profile, success criteria + fallback UX expectation.
  - Timebox: 72-hour initial smoke -> 7-day pilot window -> decision checkpoint.

Slide 3 — Prioritized checklist (Ops deliverables):
  1) Provisioned GPU pool (min specs + fallback tier).
  2) Network path validated to customer VPC (VPN or VPC peering).
  3) KMS keys available and access granted.
  4) Observability: token-level traces enabled for pilot routes, retention 7d.
  5) Canary policy configured (percent, ramp, duration).
  6) Cost guardrails: burst cap and alert thresholds.

Slide 4 — SE quick checklist (customer-facing):
  - Business objective (1 sentence).
  - Target requests/sec, p50/p95 latency goals.
  - Representative prompt set (10–20 items) and failure cases.
  - Quality KPI (accuracy/recall/ROUGE/embedding-similarity threshold).
  - Fallback UX (what user sees on degraded model).

Slide 5 — Canary policy templates (ops-config snippets) — simple presets:
  - Conservative: 5% traffic -> 1h -> rollback if error_rate > 2% or p95 > SLO.
  - Balanced: 20% -> 3h -> rollback triggers include regressed quality on seed prompts.
  - Aggressive: 50% -> 24h -> used only with Enterprise reserved capacity.
  NOTES: Map these to customer risk appetite.

Slide 6 — Simple SLO calculator (ops + se, one-liner):
  - Input: target_rps, avg_tokens_per_request, model_cost_per_1k_tokens, pilot_hours.
  - Output: estimated_token_cost = target_rps * avg_tokens_per_request * 3600 * pilot_hours / 1000 * model_cost_per_1k_tokens.
  - Quick example: 10 rps * 300 tokens * 24h on a 1.5$/k = ~6480$.
  TODO: embed spreadsheet link for live calc.

Slide 7 — Fallback ladder (operational sequence):
  1) Detect: alert on error and latency SLO breaches.
  2) Short-circuit: route to cached responses or smaller/quantized model variant.
  3) Notify SE + customer.
  4) Rollback traffic split back to stable model.
  5) Postmortem: auto-attach trace IDs and sample prompts to ticket.

Slide 8 — Short demo script for SEs (3min rapid):
  - 0:00 — One-line customer outcome.
  - 0:30 — Show current latency & cost snapshot (pre-pilot).
  - 1:00 — Launch smoke: run 5 seed prompts + show logs/kv-cache hit.
  - 2:00 — Flip canary to 10% and show metric delta.
  - 2:45 — Explain fallback behavior and rollback button.

Slide 9 — Common objections + suggested responses (ops-aware):
  Q: "What if private network adds 200ms?" -> A: Pre-validate route, enable local batching adjustment, run short latency-bound canary.
  Q: "How do we control costs during growth?" -> A: Reserved baseline + burst cap; enable token-level alerts and auto-throttle.

Slide 10 — Persona vignettes (to tailor messaging):
  - Platform Engineer (PE): wants deterministic throughput & observability. Highlight reserved capacity and tracing hooks.
  - Security/Compliance Lead: wants KMS, private control plane, audit logs. Emphasize Private deployment and HSM options.
  - Product Manager: cares about user experience and quality regressions. Show prompt-level eval and rollback windows.

Slide 11 — Rapid pilot decision rubric (go/no-go at day 7):
  - Go if: latency within agreed SLO, quality KPI met on seed set, and cost within 125% of estimate.
  - Needs follow-up if: degraded quality but stable latency (plan: A/B test prompts + quantized model).
  - Stop if: repeated production errors or customer regulator objection unresolved.

Slide 12 — Ops runbook snippets (copyable):
  - How to force a rollback (CLI + console steps).
  - How to increase canary from 10->20% safely.
  - How to attach KV-cache snapshot to ticket for SE review.
  (Keep these as short bullet commands; link to full runbook in Confluence.)

Slide 13 — Measurement plan (what to capture during pilot):
  - Perf: p50/p95/p99 latency, infra CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth.
  - Quality: seed-prompt accuracy, user acceptance % (if available).
  - Cost: tokens generated, effective $/k tokens, burst spend.
  - Ops: number of manual interventions and mean time to rollback.

Slide 14 — Open questions / TODOs:
  - Should we standardize a single canary template for mid-market vs enterprise? (ops + pricing tradeoffs)
  - Add a one-click pilot-cost estimator to Console.
  - Decide retention policy for token-level traces for pilots (privacy vs debugging).

Slide 15 — Notes to self / next steps:
  - Convert SLO calculator into playground notebook (Marco).
  - Draft concise one-pager for SE playbook (Sofia).
  - Sync with infra on GPU pool SLAs (Jon).
  - Collect 3 pilot postmortems to iterate this deck.

Appendix — example logs & sample trace snippet (redacted)
  - include sample error trace ids, sample prompt and model response mismatches for SE review.

End of deck — feedback welcome: drop comments in thread jira:GT-872 or ping #pilot-ops channel.
